_meta.description: Reference dataset of packaging material barrier and cost properties used by the recommendation engine. OTR/WVTR values are typical literature ranges for common commercial gauges, not measurements of a specific supplier's product — real performance varies with resin grade, orientation, coatings, and test conditions (temperature/RH). Treat as directional, not a spec sheet.

units.otr: cm3 / m2 / day / atm, typically measured near 23C, 0% RH unless noted
units.wvtr: g / m2 / day, typically measured near 38C, 90% RH unless noted
units.estimated_cost_per_kg_inr: Indian Rupees per kg of the FINISHED material itself (converted product, not raw resin alone), based on general/typical Indian packaging-material market pricing patterns as of dataset creation — not a live quote, not a specific supplier's price, and not adjusted for order volume. See cost_confidence and _cost_note per material.
units.material_weight_multiplier: Dimensionless — how many times more mass of this material a package typically needs vs. a standard thin flexible film baseline (~1.0), purely from format/density (rigid vs. flexible, thick vs. thin). A rough directional factor grounded in general format/density reasoning and this file's own thickness_range_micron values, NOT precise engineering/weight data. Applied on top of rules.json's packaging_weight_g_per_kg_product_by_category when computing estimated_cost_per_unit_inr — see engine/recommender.py's _estimate_packaging_cost_per_unit. See weight_multiplier_confidence and _weight_multiplier_note per material.

confidence_levels.high: Consistent across most references for standard commercial gauges
confidence_levels.medium: Typical range, but varies meaningfully by grade/orientation/supplier
confidence_levels.low: Rough estimate; highly formulation- or application-dependent

_meta.breathable: true only for materials specifically engineered/formatted for active produce ventilation (perforations or vents), not just materials whose plain resin happens to be numerically permeable. Used by the recommender's respiration_class_packaging_boost rule.
_meta.display_name_hi: Hindi display name for this material, shown in the UI when Hindi is selected. The underlying 'id' stays in English/ASCII always.

materials.name: LDPE (Low-Density Polyethylene)
materials._cost_note: Tracks polyethylene resin cost, a globally traded and fairly volatile commodity feedstock; finished film (converted, printed) sits above raw resin price.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Standard thin flexible film — the baseline this multiplier is defined against.
materials.recyclability_rating: Recyclable (resin code 4), mostly via store drop-off, not standard curbside in most regions

materials.name: HDPE (High-Density Polyethylene)
materials._cost_note: Similar commodity-resin volatility to LDPE; bottle/bag conversion adds to raw resin cost.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Spans a real format range from thin bags (near baseline) to semi-rigid bottles/jugs (heavier); category tag alone doesn't distinguish which format a given use case is, hence the wide range.

materials.name: PET (Polyethylene Terephthalate)
materials._cost_note: Resin cost plus bottle/tray conversion (blow-molding or thermoforming); bottle-grade PET resin is generally priced close to other commodity plastics.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Spans thin film/trays through bottles, similar to HDPE's format ambiguity — see vented_pet_clamshell for the dedicated rigid-tray case, which is priced separately rather than folded into this range.

materials.name: Vented PET clamshell
materials._cost_note: Same PET resin base as plain PET, but thermoforming plus the venting/perforation step is a more specialized process with less published market pricing data than commodity plastics.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Always a rigid, thick-gauge tray format (250-500 micron here vs. plain PET's mostly-thinner range) — less format ambiguity than plain PET, so a narrower, higher-confidence multiplier than the shared 'rigid_or_film' category tag alone would suggest.
materials.recyclability_rating: Widely recyclable curbside (resin code 1), same stream as standard PET
typical_use_cases: other high-respiration produce needing rigid protection plus airflow

materials.name: PP (Polypropylene)
materials._cost_note: Commodity polyolefin resin, similar volatility profile to LDPE/HDPE.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Same format ambiguity as HDPE — thin snack-bag film through rigid tubs/containers.
materials.recyclability_rating: Recyclable via specialty stream (resin code 5), limited curbside acceptance

materials.name: Metalized film (metalized BOPP/PET)
materials._cost_note: Metallization (vacuum deposition onto base BOPP/PET film) is an added processing step, the main driver of the premium over plain film.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Very thin laminate (15-40 micron here) — close to the flexible-film baseline; the metallized layer adds negligible mass.
materials.recyclability_rating: Not typically recyclable (thin metal layer on plastic substrate contaminates plastics recycling streams)
typical_use_cases: confectionery wrap requiring light + O2 barrier

materials.name: Aluminum foil laminate
materials._cost_note: Aluminum content is priced against global metals markets, historically the most volatile input of any material here, plus multilayer lamination processing cost.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Thin laminate (20-100 micron here), but aluminum is denser than typical polymer film per micron, nudging this slightly above the plain-film baseline.
materials.recyclability_rating: Not typically recyclable (multi-layer foil/plastic/paper laminate, hard to separate)

materials.name: Biodegradable / PLA film
materials._cost_note: India largely imports PLA resin rather than producing it domestically, so pricing carries import-duty and currency exposure on top of base biopolymer cost — a wider, less certain range than the commodity plastics.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Thin flexible film (20-60 micron here), assumed close to the plastic-film baseline density; less reference data for this format specifically.
materials.recyclability_rating: Industrially compostable (needs municipal composting facility); not recyclable with conventional plastics

materials.name: Micro-perforated film
materials._cost_note: Same base resin (PP or PE) as plain film plus a perforation step; limited market pricing data specific to this format versus plain LDPE/PP.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Thin flexible film (20-40 micron here), assumed close to baseline; perforation itself removes material rather than adding it.
materials.recyclability_rating: Follows base polymer (usually PP or PE film), typically limited curbside acceptance
typical_use_cases: fresh produce bags needing controlled respiration/humidity venting

materials.name: EVOH film (as multilayer barrier layer)
materials._cost_note: EVOH is a specialty barrier resin priced well above commodity plastics, typically used as a thin co-extruded layer within a multilayer structure; this range is for the finished laminate structure, not pure EVOH resin alone.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Used as a very thin co-extruded layer (5-25 micron here) within a larger flexible laminate structure — treated as close to the flexible-film baseline overall, same framing as this material's _cost_note.
materials.recyclability_rating: Not recyclable alone; used as a thin co-extruded layer within a multilayer laminate, complicating recycling of the whole structure
typical_use_cases: MAP trays needing a strong O2 barrier

materials.name: Oriented Nylon / BOPA
materials._cost_note: Nylon (polyamide) resin costs more than commodity polyolefins, plus the orientation/lamination process; limited India-specific market pricing data available.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Thin flexible film (15-25 micron here), assumed close to the plastic-film baseline density.
materials.recyclability_rating: Not typically recyclable when laminated with other polymers (common usage)

materials.name: Glass (jar/bottle)
materials._cost_note: Raw container glass is inexpensive per kg — glass's high overall packaging cost in practice comes from needing far more kg of material per unit packaged (weight) plus transport/breakage logistics, not from a high per-kg material price. See packaging_format_practicality in rules.json for that separate cost factor.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Dramatically thicker/denser than any film format (1000-4000 micron here) — the direction and rough magnitude of glass needing far more material mass per kg of product is well-established general packaging knowledge, even without precise engineering data for a specific jar/bottle design.
materials.recyclability_rating: Widely recyclable curbside, infinitely recyclable without quality loss

materials.name: Paperboard (uncoated carton board)
materials._cost_note: Depends heavily on pulp source; recycled-content board (common for secondary packaging) trends toward the lower end of this range.
materials._weight_multiplier_note: Rigid box/carton format, thicker than any film (180-600 micron here), but paper is much less dense than glass or PET, so the mass multiplier lands well below the rigid-tray/glass range — highly dependent on the specific box design.
materials.recyclability_rating: Widely recyclable curbside if uncoated; coated/laminated board is less recyclable and often needs specialty streams
typical_use_cases: cartons paired with an inner film liner for barrier
